This is T1 on a part-to-part clearance. bump = 1.002 parks the E strap 1.002 mm over the carriage, 0.002 mm past the model's 1 mm non-adjacent jam floor. The floor binds on the everyday clip frames: the 15 lowest clearances are all clip frames at 1.002 mm. On the bench, 112 taken poses sit below 1.1 mm, 182 below 1.2 mm and 284 below 2 mm (ws 61 / 110 / 185). Held: 270 below 1.1 mm and 400 below 1.2 mm. A 0.2 mm tolerance costs +0.12: bump 1.2 reads 14.88 with 0 jams. The physical clash risk is low: the same strap clears by 0.93 mm at delta 5.0, so this is the edge of the rule, not contact. The number is about 0.12 better than it would be with any build margin.

The pick sits at a cliff edge. delta 4.5 is 0.5 deg (0.70 mm of carriage arc at R_t 80.6 mm) from a cliff. delta 5.0 reads 27.53 (37 E-over-carriage jams, follow 0.88). delta 6 reads 119.05 (211 jams). ds 34 at delta 4.5 reads 47.80 (77 jams). The offset is the row's namesake, yet it buys 0.03: envsel 15.64 -> 15.61, and on the claim bench without the coil 14.26 -> 14.23. The cliff is therefore not buying score. It does mean that a 0.7 mm build or assembly error moves the model's reading by 12.8 points, so the claim has no robustness margin in this parameter. The cliff comes from the 1 mm rule (0.93 mm clearance at delta 5.0), not from metal-on-metal.

The relay's return spring is unmeasured on this hardware. R17 is inherited from proxtrack: preload 0.063 N.m, coil F >= 0.79 N. The gravity check (docs/concepts/models/armarc-relay-knuckle-4r.py:455) uses only the chain masses and the relay axis. The axis, PHI and chain are the same here, so the inheritance holds for what it measures. It does not include the carriage, bracket or coil masses, and it does not include friction. Not measured: whether the 14 mm T-nut carriage returns to its zero dowel under a 0.79 N constant-force coil against iglidur tape while the cuff loads the pad. As arithmetic only, at mu 0.2 a radial pad load of about 4 N would already stall it. Also not measured: the 3 bistable relay poses (<= ~0.8) the verifier lists as inherited and unpriced. If the carriage does not return, the zero-end poses (the lead's 4 contacts and the fold) are worn with the carriage open: a hysteresis that the static bench and the kinematic flood cannot see (G2 / G3 class).
